Resolves #19052

Installing engine `dev` as an npm dependency failed with exit 127: `package.json` ran `neo-agent-skills-materialize` from `postinstall`, a hook npm fires inside every consumer's install, where this package's devDependencies do not exist. The materializer now runs from `prepare`, which a registry or tarball install never runs ([npm v11 scripts](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/using-npm/scripts/); Git-dependency and linked-folder installs do, and neither is a supported way to consume `neo.mjs`) — `buildScripts/util/prepare.mjs` resolves each stage's bin from its package manifest and runs husky, then the materializer, behind the unchanged lock-only guard. 13.2.0 would have been the first published version carrying the hook, so no user has hit it.

Evidence: L3 (real npm lifecycle: pack → install into an empty consumer, and a bare `npm ci` in a clean worktree) → L3 required (AC-2 and AC-3 are install-lifecycle behaviors). No residuals.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `package.json` diff (no `postinstall`); `prepare.spec.mjs` › "husky runs, then the skills materializer" asserts both bins, resolved from their manifests, in order |
| AC-2 | outside-CI: `npm pack --ignore-scripts` at `ad12ecad08` → `npm install <tgz>` in an empty consumer → exit 0. The same probe on `dev@e66b6f8142` → exit 127 (`neo-agent-skills-materialize: command not found`) |
| AC-3 | outside-CI: bare `npm ci` in a clean worktree at `ad12ecad08` → "materialized 37 link(s)"; `npx --no-install neo-agent-skills-materialize --check` → exit 0 (v0.1.14). Lock-only: `prepare.spec.mjs` › "the lock-only guard short-circuits BEFORE anything runs" (zero spawns) |
| AC-4 | `prepare.spec.mjs` › "a materializer failure fails the install", "a husky failure fails the install before the materializer runs", "a manifest without the named bin entry is a named error, even when it declares others" |

## Deltas from ticket
- **Successor correction to `#17798` AC-2, Engine only:** that AC put the materializer in `postinstall` for the Engine, the Brain and devindex; the Engine alone moves to `prepare`. The Brain's and devindex's hooks, the consumer-owned projection and `--check` stand. Recorded as #19052's Decision Record impact.
- **Behaviour removed, disclosed:** on `dev`, a consumer that declares `neo-agent-skills` itself gets the skills projected into its root by the engine's hook (measured: 37 links). After this PR it gets none until it runs the materializer itself — #17798's consumer contract. `create-app` picks that line up with its devDependency sync (neomjs/create-app#34). Keeping projection as an engine feature, guarded on the package resolving, was the alternative; @neo-gpt's read (requested at @tobiu's suggestion) chose consumer-owned — the root projection was an incidental cross-package write, not a consumer contract. Recorded on #19052.
- `resolveHuskyBin` became `resolvePackageBin(packageName, binName, root)` and no longer falls back to a manifest's *first* bin when the named one is missing — `neo-agent-skills` declares nine bins, so that fallback would silently run the wrong tool.

## Test Evidence
- Consumer install, red → green: exit 127 on `dev`, exit 0 on this branch (AC-2 row).
- Own-checkout lifecycle: bare `npm ci` materializes 37 links, `--check` green, `core.hooksPath` unchanged (AC-3 row).
- Mutation: dropping the `materialize` stage fails 2 of 11 specs; restored, 11/11.
- Consumer shapes, `dev` → this branch: `create-app`'s scaffold as generated today, exit 127 → exit 0 (the nested `npm i` materializes 37 links inside `node_modules/neo.mjs`); a workspace declaring `neo-agent-skills` itself, exit 0 with 37 root links → exit 0 with none. Full table on #19052.
